flagged.evidence: The Remark says the construction achieves rate 1/32. The Definition sets the rate of C_k to k/N(k). At k=2, the construction pads to Km=4 bits (m=2) and outputs 16qm=128 bits, so its rate is 2/128=1/64, not 1/32.

The Definition says multilinearization leaves the degree in every other variable the same. For P=(X_i^2-X_i)X_j^2+X_j, both specializations at X_i=0,1 equal X_j, so R_{X_i}P=X_j; the degree in X_j drops from 2 to 1.

Step 1.1 divides by M, the number of constraints, without handling M=0. The cited constraint-graph definition sets the value of an empty edge list to 1, so its unsatisfaction remains 0 after repetition; the conclusion holds, but this step does not cover that case.

The final sentence extends the rejection estimate to any test whose outcome uses c self-corrected values, without requiring a lower bound on the corresponding ideal test's rejection probability. A test that always accepts is a function of one self-corrected value and rejects with probability 0 when the table is exactly linear, contradicting the natural reading of the claimed 1/4-minus-error estimate.

The proof says E depends only on auxiliary points and is independent of (r,s). The cited definition gives Corr_f(x;y)=f(y)+f(x+y), so correctness depends on the requested point x as well as y. The conclusion follows instead from Pr[ideal reject and E] >= Pr[ideal reject] - Pr[E^c], making this a short proof gap.

The step uses 2N <= 24TD+2. For n=0, T=0 and N=2, so this becomes 4 <= 2, which is false. The protocol sets p=3 for T=0, while the cited prime-search lemma assumes T>=1; handling this endpoint directly leaves the runtime conclusion intact.

The cited code-family definition sets rate to k/N(k). At k=2, m=2 and Km=4, so padding a 2-bit input gives a 128-bit output and rate 2/128=1/64, contradicting the Statement's rate-at-least-1/32 claim. Proof 2.1 computes Km/N(k), the rate of the full concatenated code, rather than that of the padded k-bit family.

The item infers encoded length m_k=O(k) from k+2 syntax nodes, but def-quantified-boolean-formula-and-tqbf permits any fixed effective encoding. An allowed encoding with explicit binary names x_1,...,x_k has quantifier prefix length Theta(k log k), so the stated O(k) claim is false. A specified polynomial-size encoding bound is needed for the intended degree conclusion.
